- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward trends), apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overestimating continuation.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.25) and forecast is erratic, smooth the forecast curve by averaging adjacent values to reduce noise.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.1) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 10–15% above the 14-day moving average to avoid overbought bias.
